Boyz N The Hood (1991)
Boyz n the Hood follows Tre Styles, a young Black man growing up in South Central Los Angeles under the guidance of his father, Furious Styles. After moving in with his father as a child, Tre grows up alongside his friends Ricky and Doughboy, experiencing the realities of their neighborhood while trying to figure out what kind of future he wants for himself. 

Pop culture-wise, Boyz n the Hood became one of the most influential films ever, and helped establish John Singleton as a major filmmaker. At just 23 years old, Singleton became the youngest person, and the first African-American, to be nominated for an Academy Award for Best Director at the time. 

Culturally, Boyz n the Hood was important because it gave mainstream audiences a window into everyday life in South Central Los Angeles. It showed the neighborhood as more than violence, it showed fathers raising their sons, mothers protecting their children, friends growing up together, kids playing sports, people trying to get an education, and communities dealing with circumstances that were bigger than any individual person. At the same time, it confronted serious issues surrounding gang violence, gun violence, poverty, racism, fatherhood, and the lack of opportunities available to many young Black men.
